fields.title: Where Excess Money Usually Hides
fields.keyTakeaway: In a typical infrastructure, 20–35% is spent on unused resources, and the first audit recovers most of it without product compromises.
fields.sections/0/blocks/0/text: How much of the infrastructure bill is wasted and where to look for it?
fields.sections/1/blocks/0/text: In a typical infrastructure, 20–35% of expenses go toward unused resources. This is money that can be recovered without a single product compromise, and usually no one looks for it because the bill grows slowly and raises no questions.
fields.sections/2/blocks/0/text: Five places where excess usually hides.
fields.sections/2/blocks/1/text: **[[idle-resources|Idle resources]].** Environments spun up for an experiment and forgotten. Replicas left over after migration. The first thing to check and usually the most fruitful.
fields.sections/2/blocks/2/text: **Low [[utilization|utilization]].** Capacity provisioned for peak, and peak is 3x higher than average. Autoscaling and [[spot-instances|spot instances]] for background tasks help partially.
fields.sections/2/blocks/3/text: **Storage without a retention period.** Logs, backups, old data—a direct consequence of lacking retention from `DS2-N6`. Grows unnoticed and constantly.
fields.sections/2/blocks/4/text: **Inter-zone and inter-region traffic.** Billed separately and often unexpectedly large if services are placed poorly.
fields.sections/2/blocks/5/text: **Suboptimal pricing model.** [[reserved-capacity|Reserved capacity]] is cheaper than hourly by 30–50% for predictable baseline load. Requires a one-year commitment, but the baseline load is predictable almost always.
fields.sections/2/blocks/6/text: Audit order by return: idle resources, pricing model, storage, utilization, traffic.
fields.sections/2/blocks/7/text: [[finops|FinOps]] practice boils down to a simple rule: **expenses have an owner, and they see the figure regularly.** Without this, savings are one-off.
fields.sections/3/blocks/0/text: The first audit yielded 22% savings in two weeks.
fields.sections/3/blocks/1/rows/0/0: Three test environments unused for 4 months
fields.sections/3/blocks/1/rows/3/0: Moving baseline load to reserved capacity
fields.sections/3/blocks/2/text: Out of 1.35M—306k per month, 3.7M a year, for two weeks of work by one person.
fields.sections/3/blocks/3/text: Next, we introduced a monthly review: 15 minutes at the team meeting, expense chart by drivers, anomalies discussed. Over half a year, additionally found 90k.
fields.sections/3/blocks/4/text: A separate finding: inter-zone traffic was 40k a month because the order service and database ended up in different zones after one of the moves. Moving back—an hour of work.
fields.sections/4/blocks/0/text: Savings have a limit, and after the first audit, returns drop sharply. Turning it into a permanent full-time activity is not worth it: 15 minutes a month is enough.
fields.sections/5/blocks/0/text: In a typical infrastructure, 20–35% is spent on unused resources, and the first audit recovers most of it without product compromises.
